data: The Strongmanand the Fakir: Understanding the Populist Phenomenon

How do we understand contemporary events such as Brexit, the surge in radical right political parties, left-wing anti-austerity movements, and the rise of ‘strongman’ leaders such as Donald Trump, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Narendra Modi? Connecting these phenomena is the concept of Populism that has emerged as a buzzword in contemporary times and holds a relevance that cuts across geographical boundaries. This course discusses the different theoretical approaches to populism such as the ideational approach, the discursive approach, and the performative approach. The course also offers an empirical and contextualised focus on the varying incarnations of populism and populist leaders in global politics. It pays particular attention to the gendered content of populism as a phenomenon and the field of populism studies. The course also explores different approaches to understanding populism’s relationship with democracy, and traces possible responses to the ‘populist challenge’.
